name: High-ROAS Vertical & Horizontal Campaign Scaling
purpose: Scale top-performing campaigns across Google, Meta, and TikTok vertically (gradual budget increases) and horizontally (creative & audience expansion) without resetting platform machine learning.
triggerConditions: Campaign ROAS exceeds target benchmark by > 20% over 7 consecutive days
Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) is at least 25% below client ceiling
User prompt requesting to scale winners
prerequisites: Campaign has exited initial learning phase (> 50 conversions in last 7 days)
Client monthly budget cap has remaining headroom to support scale
Supply chain / client service capacity confirmed adequate to fulfill increased volume

executionSteps.name: Identify Scaling Candidates
executionSteps.action: Filter all active campaigns maintaining ROAS >= target + 20% with healthy impression share headroom

executionSteps.name: Execute Vertical Budget Scale (+15% to +20%)
executionSteps.action: Increase daily budget by exactly 15% to 20% on winning campaigns (strictly <= 20% every 48-72 hours to prevent learning reset)

executionSteps.name: Execute Horizontal Expansion
executionSteps.action: Duplicate top-performing ad sets into new lookalike segments (1-3% LAL) or broad audiences with fresh creative angles

executionSteps.name: Deploy Budget Protection Guardrails
executionSteps.action: Set automated rule: if scaling campaign daily CPA spikes > 35% above baseline over 48 hours, immediately rollback budget

executionSteps.name: Human Approval Gate
executionSteps.action: Require explicit confirmation from marketer before scaling total daily budget past threshold

successCriteria: Conversion volume scales proportionally with <= 15% CPA degradation
Zero campaigns reset into 'Learning Limited' status
Total spend remains strictly within client monthly budget cap

failureHandling.retryStrategy: Retry budget update once on rate limit; abort if account spend cap reached

rollbackStrategy: Automatically revert daily budget to pre-scaling baseline and pause horizontal duplicate ad sets if ROAS drops below break-even.
